rationale: Two confirmed defects block approval: (1) disabled href items stay in the Tab sequence (CR-001), which can break AC1's 'first enabled, tabbable item' guarantee; (2) `closeOnFocusOut={false}` was added to `FloatingFocusManager` but is not part of the approved spec/plan and is untested, risking a dismissal regression under AC5 (CR-002). A third gap (CR-003) leaves other NavigationMore consumers using `childrenFirst`/custom children untested against the new focus manager, which the acceptance lens scored 'partial' for AC6. Three additional points raised by the blind/edge-case lenses were reviewed and dismissed: the ARIA role=menu-vs-Tab-navigation semantic question is the spec's deliberate, already-approved design choice, not a new defect; Escape-to-close/focus-return is pre-existing, unchanged, and already covered by a passing test; and the edge-case lens's 'items shrink to empty while open' finding cited a `useEffect` guard that does not exist anywhere in the diff or the current file — treated as unverifiable/hallucinated and discarded. Missing Shift+Tab test coverage is noted as a deferred coverage gap, not a blocking defect. All three lenses ran successfully (blind, edge-case, acceptance); confidence is low because of the open decision_needed item (CR-002) and the partial AC5/AC6 acceptance results.
follow_ups: Add `tabIndex={-1}` (or an equivalent means of removal from the tab sequence) to disabled href/Link items so they are skipped by Tab/initialFocus the same way disabled buttons are

Confirm the intent of `closeOnFocusOut={false}` against the approved spec (which specifies only `context`, `modal={false}`, `initialFocus={0}`) — either justify and document it with a test proving the popup still becomes non-interactive/hidden when focus moves out via Tab, or remove it to match the approved design
Add at least one test exercising `childrenFirst` / custom-children consumers with the new `FloatingFocusManager` wrap to close the AC6 coverage gap
Consider adding Shift+Tab backward-navigation coverage (non-blocking, deferred)

findings.summary: Disabled href/Link menu items remain in the Tab sequence, unlike disabled buttons.
findings.evidence: NavigationMore.tsx:190-215 — the href branch sets aria-disabled, pointer-events-none, and opacity-50 on a disabled item but never sets tabIndex={-1} (contrast with the button branch at line 227, which uses the native `disabled` attribute to remove it from the tab order). With FloatingFocusManager's initialFocus={0} and modal={false} relying on actual tabbable DOM nodes, a disabled Link as the first menu entry would still receive initial focus or remain reachable via Tab.
findings.impact: Breaks AC1 ('focus moves to the first enabled, tabbable item') and AC2 ('disabled items... skipped') whenever a disabled href item is present, especially as the first item. No existing or new test covers Tab/initial-focus against a disabled href item in that position — the only disabled-href test (NavigationMore.test.tsx:135-149) checks click behavior, not focus/tab order.
findings.recommendation: Add tabIndex={-1} (and keep aria-disabled) to disabled href items so they are excluded from the tab sequence the same way disabled buttons are, then add a test asserting Tab/initialFocus skip a disabled href item.

findings.summary: `closeOnFocusOut={false}` was added to FloatingFocusManager without appearing in the approved spec or plan, and is untested.
findings.evidence: NavigationMore.tsx:143 sets `closeOnFocusOut={false}` on FloatingFocusManager. spec.md's Design section and plan.md Step 3's code block both specify only `context={context} modal={false} initialFocus={0}` — closeOnFocusOut is absent from both approved artifacts. The only test touching this path (NavigationMore.test.tsx:338-356, 'moves focus out of the popup when tabbing past the last item (non-modal)') asserts only that focus lands on the external 'After' button; it never asserts the popup itself closes, hides, or becomes non-interactive.
findings.impact: Potential AC5 regression: a sighted keyboard user who tabs past the last item moves focus away, but the floating panel may remain visibly rendered and interactive-looking with no indication it is stale, since closeOnFocusOut normally drives FloatingFocusManager's own close-on-blur behavior and this disables it. Whether useDismiss's own focus-outside handling fully substitutes for this is not evidenced by the diff or tests.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) remove `closeOnFocusOut={false}` to match the approved design exactly, or (b) if intentionally needed to avoid a conflict with `useDismiss`, document the reason in the spec/plan and add a test proving the popup closes or becomes non-interactive once focus leaves it via Tab.

findings.summary: No test coverage for `childrenFirst` or custom-children NavigationMore consumers under the new FloatingFocusManager wrap.
findings.evidence: NavigationMore.tsx:142-158 — `childrenFirst` can render `children` before `visibleItems` inside the FloatingFocusManager-wrapped panel, and `hasMenuContent` can be true from `children` alone with no `items`. NavigationMore.test.tsx only exercises `makeItems()`-based scenarios; no test renders `childrenFirst` or passes non-trivial custom `children`.
findings.impact: AC6 ('no regression for other NavigationMore consumers') cannot be confirmed for consumers that rely on childrenFirst or custom children (acceptance lens scored this criterion 'partial' for the same reason) — if such content is non-focusable or absent, initialFocus={0} has no tabbable target and focus could land outside the intended trap.
findings.recommendation: Add at least one test rendering NavigationMore with childrenFirst and/or non-trivial custom children, asserting initial focus still lands on a sensible, focusable element.
